data.name: Vitamin Girl / ビタミンガール
data.detailed_description:
An old legendary hero, Sepsiman, was called to save the world from the evil hands of Kokoman, who wants to spread the Koko Cola disease around the world, making everyone Koko Cola Zombies!
Kokoman was too strong, Sepsiman is defeated by him and his disciple Kokogirl, the entire world was covered in Koko Cola, but one girl survived, she was immune to the cola disease! Quickly Sepsiman approaches this girl and gave her the power to transform into a "soda girl" with his Sepsi bracelet.

WHAT HAPPENED?! Instead of a soda girl, she cleansed the toxins of the Sepsi Soda and became VITAMIN GIRL! Sepsiman life it's a stake anyways... sad.

Anyways, it's up to VG to cleanse the Koko Cola from this world or even this galaxy! She will clash with Kokoman and Kokogirl and cleanse the toxins running around the the world.


-Cute super hero and villain girls doing cute things
-Insane difficulty
-Arcade Mode, if you have no lives left, you have to start from the start
-Nightmare Mode, unlocked after you finish Arcade, a harder version of the game
-20 levels lovely handcrafted so the player can enjoy this ride
-10 levels in arcade mode and 10 levels in Nightmare mode
-Gallery mode, unlock concept art collecting 100/100 cans on each stage.
-Did I mention cute girls?


Vitamin Girl is a throwback to the old runner and high speed classics. Instead of a generic endless runner, VG has levels completely handmade, not an inch of this game is random generated, every level was created with care to make the player throw the controller to the screen! (Please don't do that...)
And not only that, to expand this game even more, it's made to not only run but you also have different modes, slide down the city with a Hover-board, free roam some levels, and even ride a bike!

-Vitamin A Mode: Ride your Armadillo bike, A-kun, and drive through The Soda Way to Kokoman's lair.
-Vitamin C Mode: Run, jump, slide down! Run to the goal!
-Vitamin E Mode: Ride you Hover-board and slide down through the city and other places to reach your goal!
-Vitamin D Mode: Free roam the levels and find the exit.

data.short_description: Vitamin Girl makes throwbacks to some runner and high speed classics, while making it unique and charming. Reach the end of the road in this high difficulty game, use your Vitamin powers to save the world from the Koko Cola disease, what kind of surprises will you find at the end of the road?

reviews.review:
Vitamin Girl / ビタミンガール is a colorful, eccentric, and surprisingly demanding indie action game that combines traditional arcade challenges with high-speed running, unconventional movement mechanics, and exaggerated anime-inspired humor. Developed and published by A Penguin Studio, the game takes inspiration from classic runners while introducing several distinct gameplay styles to keep the experience interesting. Beneath its cheerful presentation lies an unforgiving adventure built around precise timing, memorization, and perseverance. Although its creativity and energetic personality are appealing, inconsistent difficulty and occasionally frustrating design decisions prevent it from fully realizing its potential.

The story introduces a bizarre world threatened by Kokoman, a villain determined to spread the mysterious Koko Cola disease and transform humanity into soda-infected zombies. When the legendary hero Sepsiman is defeated by Kokoman and his accomplice Kokogirl, civilization appears doomed. However, a young girl immune to the infection becomes humanity's final hope. Sepsiman attempts to transform her into a soda-powered heroine using his special bracelet, but the transformation unexpectedly purifies the toxins and creates Vitamin Girl. This ridiculous premise establishes the game's comedic personality, favoring absurd situations and playful superhero parody over serious storytelling. While the narrative lacks substantial character development, its unusual concept provides an entertaining foundation for the action.

The gameplay distinguishes itself through handcrafted stages rather than procedurally generated environments. Every obstacle and challenge follows a predetermined arrangement, encouraging players to memorize dangerous sections and gradually improve their performance. This structure creates a satisfying sense of mastery when difficult sequences are successfully completed. However, the emphasis on trial and error can become exhausting, particularly when unexpected hazards interrupt otherwise successful attempts. The game demands concentration and quick reactions, making it more suitable for dedicated arcade enthusiasts than casual players seeking a relaxing experience.

One of its most interesting features is the inclusion of four gameplay variations. Vitamin A Mode introduces motorcycle-based challenges aboard an armadillo-themed vehicle called A-kun, emphasizing navigation and careful movement. Vitamin C Mode focuses on traditional running mechanics, requiring players to jump, slide, and avoid obstacles while racing toward the finish line. Vitamin E Mode features hoverboard sequences that demand precise positioning and well-timed jumps through hazardous environments. Vitamin D Mode changes the formula by allowing freer exploration as players search for stage exits. These variations provide welcome diversity, although their differing complexity sometimes makes the overall experience feel uneven.

Difficulty represents both the game's greatest attraction and its most significant weakness. Arcade Mode challenges players to complete stages while managing limited lives, with complete failure requiring them to restart from the beginning. This traditional approach creates tension and makes successful progression feel rewarding. Completing Arcade Mode unlocks Nightmare Mode, which introduces an even more demanding collection of challenges. The game contains 20 handcrafted stages divided equally between these modes. While this structure provides considerable replay value for determined players, the harsh penalties can discourage those who dislike repeating previously completed sections. Some challenges reward careful observation, while others risk feeling excessively punishing.

Collectibles add another layer of engagement through the inclusion of 100 cans scattered throughout each stage. Gathering every can unlocks concept artwork in the gallery, providing an additional incentive to revisit difficult environments and pursue complete mastery. This feature gives completionists meaningful secondary objectives beyond simply reaching the finish line. Nevertheless, obtaining every collectible can become particularly frustrating when combined with the game's demanding movement mechanics and limited opportunities for mistakes. The gallery rewards are enjoyable additions, but their appeal largely depends on how much patience players have for repeated attempts.

Visually, Vitamin Girl embraces bright colors, stylized characters, and an intentionally exaggerated presentation. Its anime-inspired heroine and eccentric villains complement the ridiculous storyline, creating a distinctive identity. The environments support the game's energetic atmosphere, although the overall graphical quality remains relatively modest. Developed using Unreal Engine 4, the game demonstrates creative ambition without consistently achieving technical refinement. Clear obstacle visibility is especially important in fast-paced action games, and occasional difficulties interpreting hazards can make certain challenges feel less fair. Its presentation succeeds primarily through charm and personality rather than visual sophistication.

The technical features include full controller support, Steam Cloud functionality, and 23 Steam achievements. Interface and subtitle options are available in English, Japanese, European Spanish, and Latin American Spanish. Steam Deck compatibility is currently classified as Unknown, meaning the game has not received an official Verified or Playable designation from Valve. Although controller support suggests that its control scheme may suit handheld gaming, reliable Steam Deck performance and functionality cannot be guaranteed without additional testing.

Despite its shortcomings, the game offers a distinctive experience for players who appreciate demanding arcade challenges and unconventional indie productions. Its strongest qualities include varied gameplay mechanics, carefully constructed levels, humorous storytelling, and collectible-based replayability. Unfortunately, uneven difficulty, repetitive restarts, and occasional frustrations with obstacle design weaken the overall experience. Players expecting polished movement systems and forgiving progression may struggle to appreciate its more punishing elements, while enthusiasts of classic arcade challenges may find considerable satisfaction in mastering its stages.

Overall, Vitamin Girl / ビタミンガール is an imaginative but imperfect action adventure that successfully establishes its own identity through unusual humor, colorful aesthetics, and diverse gameplay mechanics. Its ambitious structure and demanding challenges make it an interesting option for patient players willing to overcome repeated failures. However, greater consistency in difficulty balancing and smoother progression would have significantly improved its accessibility and enjoyment. It is a worthwhile curiosity for fans of retro-inspired action games, even if its execution occasionally falls short of its creative aspirations. 

Rating: 6/10
